evidence.curator_note: Book draws 2 arcs for this branch on the molecular ion (a solid fishhook from the odd electron on O into the C1-O bond, and a solid fishhook from the C1-C2 ring bond into the same C1-O bond); moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). A THIRD arc, drawn DASHED (tail on the C1-C6 ring bond, head in the same C1-O region), sits on the same structure and belongs to the C1-C6 cleavage of Eq. 9.20; the molecular ion therefore carries THREE arcs in total -- two solid and exactly ONE dashed. CORRECTION: the first draft of this note called that a dashed 'pair'. Re-measured on the native 1760x2560 scan there is only one dashed arc, because the O-radical fishhook is SOLID and is SHARED by both branches -- which is what IMS9-EQ9.20a/b already state. Ring alpha-cleavage is intramolecular, so the product is a single ring-opened distonic ion of unchanged m/z 114, not two fragments.

Book draws 2 arcs on the folded ring-opened ion (a fishhook from the odd electron at C2 reaching toward the migrating H, and a fishhook from the C6-H bond back to C2); a third hook -- the second electron of the C6-H bond staying on C6 -- is implicit and is not drawn on the page. The migrating hydrogen cannot be atom-mapped (RDKit folds explicit H into implicit H counts), so all three collapse into the single encoded move <1>, the net one-electron relocation of the radical site from C2 to C6; this is the convention already used for the McLafferty rH step of IMS4-EQ4.33. Eq. 9.19 draws the ion in a cyclic conformation to show the six-membered H-transfer transition state.

Book draws 2 arcs on the ring-opened ion after rH (a fishhook from the odd electron into the forming pi bond and a fishhook from the breaking C-C sigma bond into that same pi bond); moves <1,2> are drawn, move <3> is an implicit homolysis hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). The odd electron sits on C6, next to the C1=O+H group, so the new pi bond must form toward C5 and the C5-C4 bond is homolysed, expelling C4H9. as the neutral (written '+ C4H9' without a dot on the page).

No MOD rule is cross-linked: data/mechanisms/rule_index.json has no by_equation entry for 9.19 or 9.20 (the MOD corpus covers Chapters 4 and 8 only), and no rule elsewhere in src/data_generation/rules/ encodes alpha-cleavage of a saturated ALCOHOL radical cation. The two nearest candidates were checked against this substrate and do NOT match: IMS_4_13_1/IMS_4_13_2 ('radical induced (alpha-)cleavage for a saturated site') require [O+.] flanked by two carbons (an ether radical cation) and split the substrate into two components, whereas here O+. carries an H and the cleavage is intramolecular ring opening; IMS_4_26_1 has the same ether requirement through its [_A] placeholders (all [_A] in one rule must unify to the same element). IMS_4_17/IMS_4_17_1-3 do cleave a C-C bond at a carbinol carbon bearing [O+.], but leave the charge/odd electron on oxygen and never form the C=O+ pi bond, so they do not describe the electron flow drawn in Eq. 9.19/9.20.

Figure 9.6 on the same page is the (unlabelled-conditions) EI mass spectrum of 2-methylcyclohexanol, M+. m/z 114; the page does not restate the electron energy, and 70 eV is the book's standard EI condition. Only the m/z 57 base peak can be read quantitatively off Figure 9.6; the other fragment m/z values are printed under the schemes without abundances, so no relative_intensity is recorded for them.
